title: capacity-aware-stream-shepherd-and-structured-output-failover
author: Elena Kim
description:
Motivation: customers reported intermittent fncall stream failures and increased tail-latency when routes experience bursty ingress combined with large structured outputs (JSON blobs). This PR introduces a capacity-aware 'stream shepherd' in the gateway proxy that smooths burst windows, enforces a conservative per-route payload ceiling by default, and adds a small structured-output failover path for OpenAI-compat streaming tool/function calls. Goals: reduce tail latency, prevent proxy buffer amplification under burst, preserve structured output fidelity, and provide a safe, observable fallback for large tool responses.

What changed (high-level):
- Added a stream_shepherd subsystem that tracks per-route in-flight tokens and enforces a sliding "grace_packets" window to avoid sudden fanout spikes.
- Introduced route-level capacity score (capacity_score) computed from route SLA tier, recent latency SLO breaches, and configured reserved_egress_bytes. Routing decisions prefer routes with headroom to serve streaming fncalls.
- Reduced default max_route_payload_bytes from 2_097_152 (2MB) to 1_048_576 (1MB) and made configuration explicit on route spec.
- Implemented a structured-output failover: if a streaming payload would overflow route headroom, the gateway switches to a chunked-final-message pattern which emits a final metadata frame that points clients to a short-lived fetch URL for the full structured blob (signed, opaque). This avoids backpressure rings in the proxy while keeping the runtime deterministic.
- OpenAI-compat layer: adjusted fncall handshake to include an 'output_mode' hint; if the server responds with a large JSON, compatibility handler negotiates failover automatically.
- Observability: added metrics (shepherd.window_size, shepherd.evicted_streams, route.capacity_score, failover.count) and tracing spans to the proxy.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated by gateway flag enable_capacity_shepherd (off by default).
- Default behavior enabled for canary region and 10% of host pools for 48h.
- Pager runbook updates and metric dashboards created before wider rollout.

Backward compatibility:
- Clients that expect continuous streaming will still receive the initial stream; only when a failover is triggered will the final metadata frame be emitted and a fetch required. Fallback is compatible with our OpenAI-compat SDKs (they will fetch automatically when signed URL is present).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for shepherd window logic and capacity_score heuristics.
- Integration tests that simulate bursty ingress, large fncall JSON responses, and confirm fallbacks trigger and signed URLs are valid for 2 minutes.
- Load soak in perf-canary region with 10k concurrent streaming connections.

Related: Linear ENG-1982 tracks SLO regressions observed in September; SUP-4121 contains customer repro steps. See docs/gateway/streaming_behavior.md for operator-facing notes.
